 And the explanation: 

 Here's a summary of each change and why:

web/app.js — restoreBackendState() (+26 lines)

The core bug fix. restoreBackendState() already fetched /api/status but discarded achievement_edits and all six decision fields. Added two blocks:

achievement_edits → window.achievementEdits — restores the user's edited per-experience bullet text. The existing restoration in loadSessionFile only covered the server-restart path; this adds it to the live-session reload path (the more common case).

_savedDecisions / selectedSummaryKey / _newSkillsFromLLM — restores experience/skill/achievement/publication decisions, summary focus, and extra skills immediately during page restore, before fetchStatus() fires. Without this, review tabs rendered between restore and the first fetchStatus() call would see empty decisions and fall back to LLM defaults.

web/app.js — buildSummaryFocusSection() (-11/+12 lines)

Replaced two serial try/catch fetches with Promise.allSettled. The original code only fell back to /api/status if the /api/master-fields request threw an exception — a normal HTTP error would leave only master summaries. Now both fetches run in parallel, failures are handled independently, and session data still overwrites master data in the same order.

web/state-manager.js (-152 lines)

Removed three functions (restoreSession, restoreBackendState, loadSessionFile) that were completely shadowed by identically-named functions in app.js, which loads after state-manager.js. These were dead code — they never executed in the browser.

_**Agent (copilot/gpt-5-mini)**_

Short answer: yes — include fast, deterministic tests (unit + the HTML harness) on PRs; keep slow, infra- or credential‑dependent integration tests off PRs and run them on main/nightly.

Suggested policy
- PRs: run Python unit tests (`tests/unit`), linters/typechecks, and the HTML harness (`npm run test:integration:headless`).
- Main/nightly: run full integration suites that require the running backend or API keys (`tests/integration`), plus heavier JS E2E against the real server.
- Guard slow/credentialed tests with env checks (e.g. `LLM_API_KEY`) and skip when absent.

What to run (examples)
- Fast PR jobs:
```bash
# python unit tests
python -m pytest -q tests/unit

# JS harness (already in workflow)
npm ci
npm run test:integration:headless
```
- Full integration (main/nightly):
```bash
conda activate cvgen
python scripts/web_app.py --llm-provider github &   # start server
python -m pytest -q tests/integration
npx playwright test
```

Tradeoffs
- Pros: faster feedback on PRs, catch client regressions early, lower CI cost.
- Cons: some integration bugs only appear under full server + provider; those require scheduled or gated runs.

Next step
- I can add a `python-tests` job to the existing workflow to run unit tests on PRs and update the workflow to run full integration on `push` to `main`/on a schedule. Want me to implement that now?
